brief.text:
Design brief (Frans, 17 Nov)

Look: A (Folded paper) and C (Postcards) look best. B is the most informative but ugly. D is too hard to use.
Chosen: a blend of A and C (not C alone).
Centrepiece: a world map of current fares from CPT, colour-coded by how good each deal is.
Map: a coloured dot per city, 5-step colour scale by deal score; tap a dot for a postcard card.
Page order (phone): top 3 deals, then the panel of all tracked destinations, then the world map.
Routes at launch: about 50 international.
Devices: phone and laptop get equal care.
Version 1 features: region and price filters, a 30-day price chart per route, a watchlist of starred destinations.
Later: stub budget link.

heading.text: Paper Plane: four directions for the home screen

heading2.text: Chosen: A + C with the fare map

scale.text:
Deal colour scale (5 steps)

Great: best date 30%+ cheaper than a typical date
Good: 20 to 30%
Fair: 10 to 20%
Typical: 0 to 10%
Pricier: above a typical date

Orange means good, blue means not, so colour-blind visitors can tell the steps apart.
After 7 days of history the score switches to today's fare against the route's 30-day median.

Windhoek, Dubai, Bali, Mauritius and London use real cached fares from 17 Nov. The other cities are sample values until the 50-route list is live.
